sanskrit: api vajradharaḥ sākṣāt kim utānye dhanurbhṛtaḥ trayāṇām api lokānāṃ samartha iti me matiḥ
english: Even the wielder of the thunderbolt himself would not be capable — what then of other bowmen? He is capable of facing even the three worlds, in my judgment.

sanskrit: bhīṣme bruvati tad vākyaṃ dhṛṣṭam ākṣipya manyumān duryodhanaṃ samālokya karṇo vacanam abravīt
english: While Bhīṣma was speaking those words, Karṇa, filled with anger, boldly contradicted him; glancing at Duryodhana, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: na tan na viditaṃ brahmaṃl loke bhūtena kena cit punaruktena kiṃ tena bhāṣitena punaḥ punaḥ
english: There is nothing in this world, O brahmin, that is not known to any creature. What purpose is served by repeating the same thing again and again?

sanskrit: duryodhanārthe śakunir dyūte nirjitavān purā samayena gato 'raṇyaṃ pāṇḍuputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: For Duryodhana's sake, Śakuni defeated him at dice in former times; and Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pāṇḍu, went to the forest under the terms of the agreement.

sanskrit: na taṃ samayam ādṛtya rājyam icchati paitṛkam balam āśritya matsyānāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca pārthivaḥ
english: Without honoring that agreement, the king desires the paternal kingdom, relying on the strength of the Matsyas and the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: duryodhano bhayād vidvan na dadyāt padam antataḥ dharmatas tu mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ pradadyāc chatrave 'pi ca
english: Out of fear, O wise one, Duryodhana would not yield even a step; yet by the law of righteousness he might give the whole earth even to an enemy.

sanskrit: yadi kāṅkṣanti te rājyaṃ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ punaḥ yathāpratijñaṃ kālaṃ taṃ carantu vanam āśritāḥ
english: If they desire again the ancestral kingdom, let them fulfill the appointed time as promised, dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanasyāṅke vartantām akutobhayāḥ adhārmikām imāṃ buddhiṃ kuryur maurkhyād dhi kevalam
english: Then let them live under Duryodhana's protection, free from all fear. This unrighteous counsel they pursue out of sheer folly.

sanskrit: atha te dharmam utsṛjya yuddham icchanti pāṇḍavāḥ āsādyemān kuruśreṣṭhān smariṣyanti vaco mama
english: But if the Pāṇḍavas abandon righteousness and desire war, they will remember my words when they encounter these best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kiṃ nu rādheya vācā te karma tat smartum arhasi eka eva yadā pārthaḥ ṣaḍ rathāñ jitavān yudhi
english: Bhīṣma said: O son of Rādhā, what use are your words? You ought to remember that deed — when Pārtha alone conquered six warriors in battle.

sanskrit: na ced evaṃ kariṣyāmo yad ayaṃ brāhmaṇo 'bravīt dhruvaṃ yudhi hatās tena bhakṣayiṣyāma pāṃsukān
english: If we do not do as this brahmin has said, we shall surely be slain by him in battle and shall swallow dust.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭras tato bhīṣmam anumānya prasādya ca avabhartsya ca rādheyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having honored and appeased Bhīṣma, and having rebuked the son of Rādhā, spoke these words.

sanskrit: asmaddhitam idaṃ vākyaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt pāṇḍavānāṃ hitaṃ caiva sarvasya jagatas tathā
english: Bhīṣma, son of Shantanu, has spoken what is beneficial for us, beneficial for the Pāṇḍavas as well, and beneficial for the whole world.

sanskrit: cintayitvā tu pārthebhyaḥ preṣayiṣyāmi saṃjayam sa bhavān pratiyātv adya pāṇḍavān eva māciram
english: Having reflected, I shall send Sañjaya to the sons of Pṛthā. Let your honor now depart to the Pāṇḍavas without delay.

sanskrit: sa taṃ satkṛtya kauravyaḥ preṣayām āsa pāṇḍavān sabhāmadhye samāhūya saṃjayaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Having honored him thus, the descendant of the Kurus sent him off to the Pāṇḍavas; and summoning Sañjaya into the midst of the assembly, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca prāptān āhuḥ saṃjaya pāṇḍuputrān; upaplavye tān vijānīhi gatvā ajātaśatruṃ ca sabhājayethā; diṣṭyānagha grāmam upasthitas tvam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: They say the sons of Pāṇḍu have arrived at Upaplavya, O Sañjaya. Go there, learn of their state, and pay honor to Ajātaśatru. By good fortune, O sinless one, you have reached the town.

sanskrit: sarvān vadeḥ saṃjaya svastimantaḥ; kṛcchraṃ vāsam atadarhā niruṣya teṣāṃ śāntir vidyate 'smāsu śīghraṃ; mithyopetānām upakāriṇāṃ satām
english: Tell them all, O Sañjaya, that they are well. After dwelling in hardship unworthy of them, peace between them and us is close at hand — for those noble benefactors who have been wronged.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ kva cit saṃjaya pāṇḍavānāṃ; mithyāvṛttiṃ kāṃ cana jātv apaśyam sarvāṃ śriyaṃ hy ātmavīryeṇa labdhvā; paryākārṣuḥ pāṇḍavā mahyam eva
english: I have never, O Sañjaya, at any time observed any wrongful conduct on the part of the Pāṇḍavas. Having won all their prosperity by their own valor, the Pāṇḍavas yielded it all to me.

sanskrit: doṣaṃ hy eṣāṃ nādhigacche parikṣan; nityaṃ kaṃ cid yena garheya pārthān dharmārthābhyāṃ karma kurvanti nityaṃ; sukhapriyā nānurudhyanti kāmān
english: Searching always, I find no fault in them, however small, for which I could blame the sons of Pṛthā. They always act in accordance with righteousness and the proper ends of life; though fond of pleasure, they never pursue their desires unrestrained.

sanskrit: gharmaṃ śītaṃ kṣutpipāse tathaiva; nidrāṃ tandrīṃ krodhaharṣau pramādam dhṛtyā caiva prajñayā cābhibhūya; dharmārthayogān prayatanti pārthāḥ
english: Overcoming heat and cold, hunger and thirst, sleep and drowsiness, anger and elation, and heedlessness — through steadfastness and wisdom, the sons of Pṛthā strive for righteousness and proper purpose.

sanskrit: tyajanti mitreṣu dhanāni kāle; na saṃvāsāj jīryati maitram eṣām yathārhamānārthakarā hi pārthās; teṣāṃ dveṣṭā nāsty ājamīḍhasya pakṣe
english: They give up wealth in due season for their friends; their friendship does not wither through mere long dwelling together. The sons of Pṛthā bestow honor and benefit according to what is fitting. Among the descendants of Ajamidha, there is none who hates them.

sanskrit: anyatra pāpād viṣamān mandabuddher; duryodhanāt kṣudratarāc ca karṇāt teṣāṃ hīme hīnasukhapriyāṇāṃ; mahātmanāṃ saṃjanayanti tejaḥ
english: Except from the evil, crooked, dull-witted Duryodhana and the yet more petty Karṇa — these wretched beings who are fond of base pleasures — these great-souled ones generate their splendor.

sanskrit: utthānavīryaḥ sukham edhamāno; duryodhanaḥ sukṛtaṃ manyate tat teṣāṃ bhāgaṃ yac ca manyeta bālaḥ; śakyaṃ hartuṃ jīvatāṃ pāṇḍavānām
english: Duryodhana, thriving in comfort with energetic might, regards that as a meritorious act — and the childish one thinks the portion belonging to the Pāṇḍavas can be seized while they still live.

sanskrit: yasyārjunaḥ padavīṃ keśavaś ca; vṛkodaraḥ sātyako 'jātaśatroḥ mādrīputrau sṛñjayāś cāpi sarve; purā yuddhāt sādhu tasya pradānam
english: He who has Arjuna, Keśava, Vṛkodara, Sātyaki, Ajātaśatru, the two sons of Mādrī, and all the Sṛñjayas in his train — it is good to offer unto him before a war.

sanskrit: sa hy evaikaḥ pṛthivīṃ savyasācī; gāṇḍīvadhanvā praṇuded rathasthaḥ tathā viṣṇuḥ keśavo 'py apradhṛṣyo; lokatrayasyādhipatir mahātmā
english: For Savyasācin alone, standing in his chariot with the Gāṇḍīva bow, can drive back the whole earth; and likewise Keśava Viṣṇu is irresistible — the great-souled lord of the three worlds.

sanskrit: tiṣṭheta kas tasya martyaḥ purastād; yaḥ sarvadeveṣu vareṇya īḍyaḥ parjanyaghoṣān pravapañ śaraughān; pataṃgasaṃghān iva śīghravegān
english: What mortal could stand before him who is worthy of adoration among all the gods — he who scatters showers of arrows with the roar of rain clouds, swift as flocks of birds in flight?

sanskrit: diśaṃ hy udīcīm api cottarān kurūn; gāṇḍīvadhanvaikaratho jigāya dhanaṃ caiṣām āharat savyasācī; senānugān balidāṃś caiva cakre
english: With his single chariot and the Gāṇḍīva bow, he conquered even the northern quarter and the Northern Kurus; Savyasācin carried off their wealth and made their followers bring tribute.

sanskrit: yaś caiva devān khāṇḍave savyasācī; gāṇḍīvadhanvā prajigāya sendrān upāharat phalguno jātavedase; yaśo mānaṃ vardhayan pāṇḍavānām
english: And it was Savyasācin with his Gāṇḍīva who conquered even the gods together with Indra at Khandava, and Phalguna offered up the fire to Jātaveda, thereby increasing the glory and honor of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: gadābhṛtāṃ nādya samo 'sti bhīmād; dhastyāroho nāsti samaś ca tasya rathe 'rjunād āhur ahīnam enaṃ; bāhvor bale cāyutanāgavīryam
english: Among mace-bearers today there is none equal to Bhīma; nor is there his equal in mounting an elephant. In the chariot they say none is inferior to Arjuna, and in the strength of his arms he has the power of ten thousand elephants.

sanskrit: suśikṣitaḥ kṛtavairas tarasvī; dahet kruddhas tarasā dhārtarāṣṭrān sadātyamarṣī balavān na śakyo; yuddhe jetuṃ vāsavenāpi sākṣāt
english: Well-trained, a confirmed enemy, and valiant, when enraged he could swiftly burn up the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Ever intolerant and powerful, he cannot be defeated in battle even by Vāsava himself in person.

sanskrit: sucetasau balinau śīghrahastau; suśikṣitau bhrātarau phalgunena śyenau yathā pakṣipūgān rujantau; mādrīputrau neha kurūn viśetām
english: Keen-minded, powerful, swift of hand, well-trained by Phalguna — the two brothers, sons of Mādrī, tearing apart troops of warriors like two hawks rending flocks of birds, would let none of the Kurus escape.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhye vartamānas tarasvī; dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pāṇḍavānām ihaikaḥ sahāmātyaḥ somakānāṃ prabarhaḥ; saṃtyaktātmā pāṇḍavānāṃ jayāya
english: Moving in their midst, the valiant Dhṛṣṭadyumna is here the sole chief of the Pāṇḍavas, together with the counselors, the foremost of the Somakas, his very life surrendered for the Pāṇḍavas' victory.

sanskrit: sahoṣitaś caritārtho vayaḥsthaḥ; śālveyānām adhipo vai virāṭaḥ saha putraiḥ pāṇḍavārthe ca śaśvad; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhakta iti śrutaṃ me
english: Virāṭa, king of the Shalveyas, having achieved his purpose by dwelling with them and being of mature age, is said, along with his sons, to be always devoted to the cause of the Pāṇḍavas and to Yudhiṣṭhira — so I have heard.

sanskrit: avaruddhā balinaḥ kekayebhyo; maheṣvāsā bhrātaraḥ pañca santi kekayebhyo rājyam ākāṅkṣamāṇā; yuddhārthinaś cānuvasanti pārthān
english: Five powerful brothers, great bowmen, are kept excluded from the Kekayas and desire the Kekaya kingdom; longing for battle, they dwell with the sons of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: sarve ca vīrāḥ pṛthivīpatīnāṃ; samānītāḥ pāṇḍavārthe niviṣṭāḥ śūrān ahaṃ bhaktimataḥ śṛṇomi; prītyā yuktān saṃśritān dharmarājam
english: And all the warriors, the lords of the earth, have been assembled and have committed themselves to the cause of the Pāṇḍavas. I hear of the heroes devoted with affection, united in love, attached to Dharmarāja.

sanskrit: giryāśrayā durganivāsinaś ca; yodhāḥ pṛthivyāṃ kulajā viśuddhāḥ mlecchāś ca nānāyudhavīryavantaḥ; samāgatāḥ pāṇḍavārthe niviṣṭāḥ
english: Warriors from the mountain retreats and the residents of inaccessible places, high-born and pure throughout the world, and also barbarians powerful with various weapons, have assembled and committed themselves to the Pāṇḍavas' cause.

sanskrit: pāṇḍyaś ca rājāmita indrakalpo; yudhi pravīrair bahubhiḥ sametaḥ samāgataḥ pāṇḍavārthe mahātmā; lokapravīro 'prativīryatejāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍya king too, of boundless energy, equal to Indra, accompanied by many great warriors in battle, that great-souled one has come for the Pāṇḍavas' cause — foremost hero of the world, his valor and splendor unrivaled.

sanskrit: astraṃ droṇād arjunād vāsudevāt; kṛpād bhīṣmād yena kṛtaṃ śṛṇomi yaṃ taṃ kārṣṇipratimaṃ prāhur ekaṃ; sa sātyakiḥ pāṇḍavārthe niviṣṭaḥ
english: He who, I hear, has received weapons from Droṇa, Arjuna, Vāsudeva, Kṛpa, and Bhīṣma — him they call the only one equal to the son of Kṛṣṇa. That Sātyaki has committed himself to the Pāṇḍavas' cause.

sanskrit: apāśritāś cedikarūṣakāś ca; sarvotsāhair bhūmipālaiḥ sametāḥ teṣāṃ madhye sūryam ivātapantaṃ; śriyā vṛtaṃ cedipatiṃ jvalantam
english: And the Cedis and the Karūṣas, together with earth-lords of every valor, have taken their side; in their midst shines the lord of the Cedis, blazing with glory like the sun in splendor.

sanskrit: astambhanīyaṃ yudhi manyamānaṃ; jyākarṣatāṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ pṛthivyām sarvotsāhaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ nihatya; prasahya kṛṣṇas tarasā mamarda
english: Thinking himself unstoppable in battle, the foremost of all who draw the bowstring on earth, Śiśupāla mustered all his kingly energy — yet Kṛṣṇa violently slew him and crushed him with his might.

sanskrit: yaśomānau vardhayan yādavānāṃ; purābhinac chiśupālaṃ samīke yasya sarve vardhayanti sma mānaṃ; karūṣarājapramukhā narendrāḥ
english: Increasing the glory and honor of the Yādavas, he slew Śiśupāla in battle in former times; all the kings of the earth, headed by the lord of Karusha, used to increase his honor.

sanskrit: tam asahyaṃ keśavaṃ tatra matvā; sugrīvayuktena rathena kṛṣṇam saṃprādravaṃś cedipatiṃ vihāya; siṃhaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣudramṛgā ivānye
english: Regarding Keśava there as irresistible, the other kings, abandoning the lord of the Cedis, fled from Kṛṣṇa with his Sugrīva-yoked chariot, like small animals on seeing a lion.

sanskrit: yas taṃ pratīpas tarasā pratyudīyād; āśaṃsamāno dvairathe vāsudevam so 'śeta kṛṣṇena hataḥ parāsur; vātenevonmathitaḥ karṇikāraḥ
english: He who came swiftly against him in opposition, hoping to challenge Vāsudeva in a single-chariot duel — that one lay slain by Kṛṣṇa, his life gone, uprooted by Kṛṣṇa like a Karṇikāra tree by the wind.

sanskrit: parākramaṃ me yad avedayanta; teṣām arthe saṃjaya keśavasya anusmaraṃs tasya karmāṇi viṣṇor; gāvalgaṇe nādhigacchāmi śāntim
english: When they reported to me the prowess of Keśava for the sake of those Pāṇḍavas, O Sañjaya, reflecting on the deeds of Viṣṇu — O son of Gavalgaṇa, I find no peace.

sanskrit: na jātu tāñ śatrur anyaḥ saheta; yeṣāṃ sa syād agraṇīr vṛṣṇisiṃhaḥ pravepate me hṛdayaṃ bhayena; śrutvā kṛṣṇāv ekarathe sametau
english: No enemy could ever withstand those at whose head stands that lion of the Vṛṣṇis. My heart trembles with fear at hearing of the two Kṛṣṇas riding together in one chariot.

sanskrit: no ced gacchet saṃgaraṃ mandabuddhis; tābhyāṃ suto me viparītacetāḥ no cet kurūn saṃjaya nirdahetām; indrāviṣṇū daityasenāṃ yathaiva mato hi me śakrasamo dhanaṃjayaḥ; sanātano vṛṣṇivīraś ca viṣṇuḥ
english: Unless my dull-witted and perverse son goes to battle against those two — unless they burn up the Kurus as Indra and Viṣṇu burned the Daitya host — for in my opinion Dhanañjaya is equal to Śakra and the eternal hero of the Vṛṣṇis is Viṣṇu himself.

sanskrit: dharmārāmo hrīniṣedhas tarasvī; kuntīputraḥ pāṇḍavo 'jātaśatruḥ duryodhanena nikṛto manasvī; no cet kruddhaḥ pradahed dhārtarāṣṭrān
english: The valiant son of Kuntī, the Pāṇḍava Ajātaśatru, who delights in righteousness and is restrained by modesty — that high-minded one, deceived by Duryodhana, unless he in anger burns up the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tathā hy arjunād vāsudevād; bhīmād vāpi yamayor vā bibhemi yathā rājñaḥ krodhadīptasya sūta; manyor ahaṃ bhītataraḥ sadaiva
english: For I do not fear Arjuna, Vāsudeva, Bhīma, or the twin sons of Mādrī so much, O charioteer, as I am always more afraid of the wrath of the king blazing with anger.

sanskrit: alaṃ tapobrahmacaryeṇa yuktaḥ; saṃkalpo 'yaṃ mānasas tasya sidhyet tasya krodhaṃ saṃjayāhaṃ samīke; sthāne jānan bhṛśam asmy adya bhītaḥ
english: Endowed with austerity and celibacy aplenty, whatever mental resolve he forms would be accomplished. Knowing his wrath in battle, O Sañjaya, I am greatly afraid today — and rightly so.

sanskrit: sa gaccha śīghraṃ prahito rathena; pāñcālarājasya camūṃ paretya ajātaśatruṃ kuśalaṃ sma pṛccheḥ; punaḥ punaḥ prītiyuktaṃ vades tvam
english: So go quickly, dispatched by chariot; passing by the army of the Pāñcāla king, inquire after the welfare of Ajātaśatru, and speak lovingly to him again and again.

sanskrit: janārdanaṃ cāpi sametya tāta; mahāmātraṃ vīryavatām udāram anāmayaṃ madvacanena pṛccher; dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ śāntim īpsuḥ
english: And meeting Janārdana as well, O dear one — the greatest among the mighty, the noble one — inquire after his welfare in my name, saying: Dhṛtarāṣṭra desires peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: na tasya kiṃ cid vacanaṃ na kuryāt; kuntīputro vāsudevasya sūta priyaś caiṣām ātmasamaś ca kṛṣṇo; vidvāṃś caiṣāṃ karmaṇi nityayuktaḥ
english: The son of Kuntī would do nothing contrary to Vāsudeva's word, O charioteer; Kṛṣṇa is dear to them and regarded as their very self, and he is ever engaged in their affairs, being wise.

sanskrit: samānīya pāṇḍavān sṛñjayāṃś ca; janārdanaṃ yuyudhānaṃ virāṭam anāmayaṃ madvacanena pṛccheḥ; sarvāṃs tathā draupadeyāṃś ca pañca
english: Having assembled the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas, inquire after the welfare of Janārdana, Yuyudhāna, and Virāṭa in my name; and likewise of all the five sons of Draupadī.

sanskrit: yad yat tatra prāptakālaṃ parebhyas; tvaṃ manyethā bhāratānāṃ hitaṃ ca tat tad bhāṣethāḥ saṃjaya rājamadhye; na mūrchayed yan na bhavec ca yuddham
english: Whatever you deem timely there, on behalf of our opponents, and whatever is beneficial for the Bhāratas — all that speak out, O Sañjaya, in the assembly of kings, so that no one may faint and that there be no war.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rājñas tu vacanaṃ śrutvā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya saṃjayaḥ upaplavyaṃ yayau draṣṭuṃ pāṇḍavān amitaujasaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Sañjaya went to Upaplavya to see the Pāṇḍavas of immeasurable might.

sanskrit: sa tu rājānam āsādya dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram praṇipatya tataḥ pūrvaṃ sūtaputro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: And having reached the righteous-souled King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of the charioteer first prostrated himself and then addressed him.

sanskrit: gāvalgaṇiḥ saṃjayaḥ sūtasūnur; ajātaśatrum avadat pratītaḥ diṣṭyā rājaṃs tvām arogaṃ prapaśye; sahāyavantaṃ ca mahendrakalpam
english: Gavalgaṇa's son Sañjaya, the charioteer's grandson, addressed Ajātaśatru with confidence: 'By good fortune, O king, I see you in good health, with your allies, resembling great Indra himself.'

sanskrit: anāmayaṃ pṛcchati tvāmbikeyo; vṛddho rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro manīṣī kaccid bhīmaḥ kuśalī pāṇḍavāgryo; dhanaṃjayas tau ca mādrītanūjau
english: 'The aged king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, that wise one, inquires after your welfare. Is Bhīma, foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, in good health? And Dhanañjaya? And the two sons of Mādrī?'

sanskrit: kaccit kṛṣṇā draupadī rājaputrī; satyavratā vīrapatnī saputrā manasvinī yatra ca vāñchasi tvam; iṣṭān kāmān bhārata svastikāmaḥ
english: 'Is Kṛṣṇa Draupadī, the royal princess, that one firm in her vow, wife of heroes, together with her sons, that high-minded lady, well? And wherever you desire, O Bhārata, do you obtain your cherished wishes? May you be blessed.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gāvalgaṇe saṃjaya svāgataṃ te; prītātmāhaṃ tvābhivadāmi sūta anāmayaṃ pratijāne tavāhaṃ; sahānujaiḥ kuśalī cāsmi vidvan
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: 'O son of Gavalgaṇa, O Sañjaya, welcome to you. I greet you with a glad heart, O charioteer. I declare that I am well; and together with my brothers I am in good health, O wise one.'

sanskrit: cirād idaṃ kuśalaṃ bhāratasya; śrutvā rājñaḥ kuruvṛddhasya sūta manye sākṣād dṛṣṭam ahaṃ narendraṃ; dṛṣṭvaiva tvāṃ saṃjaya prītiyogāt
english: 'After a long time, O charioteer, hearing this welfare of the king, the aged Kuru, I consider it as if I have seen the lord of men in person — for in seeing you, O Sañjaya, I am joined with gladness.'

sanskrit: pitāmaho naḥ sthaviro manasvī; mahāprājñaḥ sarvadharmopapannaḥ sa kauravyaḥ kuśalī tāta bhīṣmo; yathāpūrvaṃ vṛttir apy asya kaccit
english: 'Our grandfather, that aged, high-minded one, supremely wise, endowed with all righteousness — is that descendant of the Kurus, Bhīṣma, in good health, O dear one? And does his conduct remain as before?'

sanskrit: kaccid rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputro; vaicitravīryaḥ kuśalī mahātmā mahārājo bāhlikaḥ prātipeyaḥ; kaccid vidvān kuśalī sūtaputra
english: 'Is King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Vicitravīrya, together with his sons, in good health, that great-souled one? Is the great king Bahlika, son of Pratīpa, in good health, that learned one, O son of a charioteer?'

sanskrit: sa somadattaḥ kuśalī tāta kaccid; bhūriśravāḥ satyasaṃdhaḥ śalaś ca droṇaḥ saputraś ca kṛpaś ca vipro; maheṣvāsāḥ kaccid ete 'py arogāḥ
english: 'Is Somadatta in good health, O dear one? And Bhūriśravas, Śalya the firm in his vows, Droṇa with his son, and Kṛpa the brahmin — are these great bowmen also free from illness?'

sanskrit: mahāprājñāḥ sarvaśāstrāvadātā; dhanurbhṛtāṃ mukhyatamāḥ pṛthivyām kaccin mānaṃ tāta labhanta ete; dhanurbhṛtaḥ kaccid ete 'py arogāḥ
english: 'Supremely wise, versed in all the sciences, the foremost of bowmen on this earth — do these receive the honor they deserve, O dear one? And are these bowmen also free from illness?'

sanskrit: sarve kurubhyaḥ spṛhayanti saṃjaya; dhanurdharā ye pṛthivyāṃ yuvānaḥ yeṣāṃ rāṣṭre nivasati darśanīyo; maheṣvāsaḥ śīlavān droṇaputraḥ
english: 'All the young bowmen on earth envy the Kurus, O Sañjaya — in whose kingdom dwells Droṇa's son, that handsome great bowman of noble character.'

sanskrit: vaiśyāputraḥ kuśalī tāta kaccin; mahāprājño rājaputro yuyutsuḥ karṇo 'mātyaḥ kuśalī tāta kaccit; suyodhano yasya mando vidheyaḥ
english: 'Is the son of a vaishya woman, that most wise royal son Yuyutsu, in good health, O dear one? Is Karṇa, the minister, in good health, O dear one — whose Suyodhana is the dull and obedient tool?'

sanskrit: striyo vṛddhā bhāratānāṃ jananyo; mahānasyo dāsabhāryāś ca sūta vadhvaḥ putrā bhāgineyā bhaginyo; dauhitrā vā kaccid apy avyalīkāḥ
english: 'The aged women, the mothers of the Bhāratas, the ladies of the kitchen, the wives of servants, O charioteer — the daughters-in-law, the sons, the nephews, the sisters, and the daughters' sons — are all of these also well?'

sanskrit: kaccid rājā brāhmaṇānāṃ yathāvat; pravartate pūrvavat tāta vṛttim kaccid dāyān māmakān dhārtarāṣṭro; dvijātīnāṃ saṃjaya nopahanti
english: 'Does the king conduct himself toward the brahmins duly, as formerly, O dear one? Does the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra fail to withhold the shares belonging to me for the twice-born ones, O Sañjaya?'

sanskrit: kaccid rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputra; upekṣate brāhmaṇātikramān vai kaccin na hetor iva vartmabhūta; upekṣate teṣu sa nyūnavṛttim
english: 'Does King Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his sons overlook the transgressions of brahmins? Does he not, as one looking after his road, overlook such deficient conduct toward them?'

sanskrit: etaj jyotir uttamaṃ jīvaloke; śuklaṃ prajānāṃ vihitaṃ vidhātrā te cel lobhaṃ na niyacchanti mandāḥ; kṛtsno nāśo bhavitā kauravāṇām
english: 'This is the supreme light in the living world, the pure brightness ordained by the Creator for the subjects. If those dull ones do not restrain their greed, the complete ruin of the Kauravas is at hand.'

sanskrit: kaccid rājā dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saputro; bubhūṣate vṛttim amātyavarge kaccin na bhedena jijīviṣanti; suhṛdrūpā durhṛdaś caikamitrāḥ
english: 'Does King Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his sons desire proper conduct in the ranks of his ministers? Do those who appear as friends but are secret enemies not seek to live by sowing division, sharing one set of allies?'

sanskrit: kaccin na pāpaṃ kathayanti tāta; te pāṇḍavānāṃ kuravaḥ sarva eva kaccid dṛṣṭvā dasyusaṃghān sametān; smaranti pārthasya yudhāṃ praṇetuḥ
english: 'Do the Kurus all not speak evil of the Pāṇḍavas, O dear one? And on seeing the assembled hosts of the enemy, do they remember Pārtha, the leader in battle?'

sanskrit: maurvībhujāgraprahitān sma tāta; dodhūyamānena dhanurdhareṇa gāṇḍīvamuktān stanayitnughoṣān; ajihmagān kaccid anusmaranti
english: 'Do they recall those arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, straight-flying, thundering like storm clouds, shot from the arm's end of the bowstring by the quivering bowman, O dear one?'

sanskrit: na hy apaśyaṃ kaṃ cid ahaṃ pṛthivyāṃ; śrutaṃ samaṃ vādhikam arjunena yasyaikaṣaṣṭir niśitās tīkṣṇadhārāḥ; suvāsasaḥ saṃmato hastavāpaḥ
english: 'For I have not seen or heard of anyone on earth equal to Arjuna or greater — he whose sixty-one sharp-edged arrows, well-feathered and well-regarded, are released with perfect hand-speed.'

sanskrit: gadāpāṇir bhīmasenas tarasvī; pravepayañ śatrusaṃghān anīke nāgaḥ prabhinna iva naḍvalāsu; caṅkramyate kaccid enaṃ smaranti
english: 'The valiant Bhīmasena, mace in hand, making hosts of enemies tremble in battle, roaming like a maddened elephant among reeds — do they remember him?'

sanskrit: mādrīputraḥ sahadevaḥ kaliṅgān; samāgatān ajayad dantakūre vāmenāsyan dakṣiṇenaiva yo vai; mahābalaṃ kaccid enaṃ smaranti
english: 'Sahadeva, son of Mādrī, who conquered the assembled Kaliṅgas at Dantakura, shooting with his left hand and his right alike — that one of great strength, do they remember him?'

sanskrit: udyann ayaṃ nakulaḥ preṣito vai; gāvalgaṇe saṃjaya paśyatas te diśaṃ pratīcīṃ vaśam ānayan me; mādrīsutaṃ kaccid enaṃ smaranti
english: 'This Nakula, when dispatched by me and rising up — even as you watched, O son of Gavalgaṇa, O Sañjaya — brought the western quarter under my sway. That son of Mādrī, do they remember him?'

sanskrit: abhyābhavo dvaitavane ya āsīd; durmantrite ghoṣayātrāgatānām yatra mandāñ śatruvaśaṃ prayātān; amocayad bhīmaseno jayaś ca
english: 'The victory that occurred in the Dvaita forest, over those who came on the ill-advised cattle-raid — where those foolish ones, fallen into the enemy's power, were freed by Bhīmasena and Arjuna the victorious.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ paścād arjunam abhyarakṣaṃ; mādrīputrau bhīmasenaś ca cakre gāṇḍīvabhṛc chatrusaṃghān udasya; svasty āgamat kaccid enaṃ smaranti
english: 'I protected Arjuna from behind, while the two sons of Mādrī and Bhīmasena formed the guard; and the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, driving off the enemy's hosts, returned safe. Do they remember that?'
